name: Domesticated maize
summary: Starch and plant-silica traces at Xihuatoxtla in Mexico's Balsas Valley show people using domesticated maize by about 6750 BCE, the beginning of a crop that later fed the Americas.
description: Human-selected maize as a cultivated crop, evidenced by starch and phytolith remains at Xihuatoxtla; distinct from later alkaline cooking.
tier_reason: The domestic crop supports subsequent food production, settlement economies and crop systems across generations; rank concerns the crop capability, not one excavation.
